messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Production streaming p99 latency breach detected for model-inference-prod (us-east-1). Trigger: p99 > 2s for 3 consecutive mins. Incident severity: P1. Auto-page sent to #oncall and #incidents.

sara_oncall: acked. I'm on it. pulling up dashboards and logs now :eyes:

sara_oncall: quick update — seeing p95 jump from ~420ms -> ~850ms, p99 ~1.9s -> 6.2s across streaming endpoints. Number of in-flight streams with stalled tokens increasing. Looks concentrated on a subset of GPU nodes in cluster gpu-pool-3.

mike_infra: I see the same. `node-exporter` shows thermal spike on node gpu-3b-07 and a stream of ECC correctable errors. Possible thermal-triggered throttle. Dumping nvml logs now.

mike_infra: nvml excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T13:02:11Z GPU: gpu-3b-07 ECC_CORRECTABLE 12
2026-03-15T13:02:12Z GPU: gpu-3b-07 THERMAL_THROTTLE TEMP=88.4C
2026-03-15T13:02:13Z GPU: gpu-3b-07 ECC_CORRECTABLE 15
```

sara_oncall: thanks. if it's thermal + ECC, streaming KV-cache stalls are likely — the KV worker hits a page stall and upstream request sits waiting for token emission. That matches the customer-reported stalls in EMEA region.

ops-bot: Customer incidents flagged: 7 customers with active streaming sessions in EMEA. Top impacted product: chat-realtime (prod). Ticket numbers: #INC-3421, #INC-3422, #INC-3423.

kevin_support: customers reporting 2-5s pauses mid-stream, some reconnects. No data loss reports, just intermittent stalls and delayed message chunks.

tara_sre: immediate mitigation options:
- evacuate gpu-3b-07 from serving pool (drain) and migrate its jobs
- enable fallback routing to smaller model variants in dedicated fallback pool
- temporarily increase per-connection timeout/retry to reduce SLO noise
Which should we run first?

mike_infra: I'm going to drain the node now (safe drain to let current batches finish) and redirect new sessions. Command:
```
rwdctl node drain --node gpu-3b-07 --mode safe
rwdctl route update --pool gpu-pool-3 --remove-node gpu-3b-07
```

sara_oncall: do it. also enable KV cache bypass for affected model(s) to avoid stalls while we migrate. low-risk toggle: `feature.kv_cache.bypass=true` for model-inference-prod-rt.

mike_infra: drain started. ETA for active sessions to finish ~45s. I'll monitor for residual stalls.

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: node drain initiated by mike_infra at 2026-03-15T13:04:20Z. Routing change queued.

sara_oncall: routing change applied, warmup on fallback pool triggered. Early telemetry: p95 improved to ~520ms within 60s, p99 trending down but still elevated around 2.8s.

jen_prod: thanks — I'm seeing reduced errors on API gateway. I'm flipping the canary to 100% on fallback for chat-realtime for the next 10m to validate.

kevin_support: informing impacted customers with ETA ~15m for full mitigation. posting note to status page: "Partial degradation for streaming chat in EMEA; mitigation underway."

mike_infra: drain complete. node shows persistent ECC correctable flood and fan RPM oscillation. Suggest hardware replacement. I'll quarantine gpu-3b-07 and request swap via vendor ticket.

mike_infra: quick hardware summary: fan duty cycles oscillating 20-95% every ~30s, GPU temp steady ~87-89C under load, ECC correctable rate high. Suspect flaky fan or thermal sensor.

tara_sre: creating an oncall handoff: @jen_prod you'll be primary for the next 2 hours to watch the fallback. I'll stay on as infra liaise until vendor acknowledges replacement.

jen_prod: taking over. I'll keep canary at 100% for 10m then step down to normal if stable. Can someone capture a targeted eval set for quality check after fallback? want to ensure model outputs unchanged.

sara_oncall: tagging @ml-evals to run quick regression on 20 representative prompts. Also enabling detailed trace logs for affected requests: `trace=on; trace-sampling=100%` for the canary window.

ops-bot: status page updated. RFC note: customers notified via email for high-impact sessions. Support team webhook posted to #support.

kevin_support: support triage note: collecting logs from 5 impacted customers, PRDs attached. No reports of corrupt output.

mike_infra: vendor ticket created: VT-9982. Requested same-day swap for thermal module. Attached nvml logs and BMC snapshots.

sara_oncall: summary for post-incident: root cause likely failing thermal control on gpu-3b-07 causing thermal throttling and elevated ECC correctables -> KV cache stalls -> p99 streaming stalls. Mitigation: drained and quarantined node, rerouted traffic to fallback pool, enabled KV-cache bypass, canary -> 100%, support notified, vendor engaged. Impact: p95 rose to ~850ms, p99 peaked ~6.2s for ~6 minutes, ~7 customers with degraded experience. No data loss.

jen_prod: noted. I'll own the follow-up: run regression checks, validate no model quality regression, coordinate vendor swap, and draft the postmortem. Owning until EOD. @tara_sre please add hardware trace and remediation steps.

tara_sre: will add. also recommend: add automatic thermal-evacuate policy if ECC_CORRECTABLE > X and TEMP > Y for > 60s to avoid hitting p99. filing enhancement: RWD-1154.

sara_oncall: thanks everyone. final status: mitigation successful, p99 back to ~300-400ms across the region after reroute and drain. handing off to @jen_prod for follow-up. Marking incident as mitigated but still active for postmortem items.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 2026-03-15T13:12:56Z. Owner: jen_prod. Severity remains P1 until postmortem completed.

jen_prod: I'll post the draft postmortem by EOD and add links to telemetry and commands run. leaving a short checklist for next oncall: verify vendor replacement and monitor for similar ECC spikes in other nodes.

kevin_support: support will keep watch on customer tickets and escalate if any regressions.

sara_oncall: great work team :clap: — closing active paging. if anyone finds related anomalies, ping the thread and we'll re-open.

ops-bot: Closed paging channel. Logs and action items archived to /incidents/8642009876/ (auto)."
